chore(task): close navigator-coverage now its pull request has landed

The lifecycle's own closing bookkeeping, left over because the frozen CLI had
no codev next to surface it after #33 merged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs(plans): fold three findings from building the measure into the DX plan

All three were surfaced by building and then using the navigator coverage
measure, not by reading code, which is the first evidence it earns its place.

_github_position is consulted only for ok_machine_review_complete, so every
other reason skips GitHub and a merged slice is still told to open a pull
request. Found on main, minutes after #33 merged, when codev next said exactly
that. Package 3.

gate.py's _SPEC_GLOBS does not cover docs/plans/*.md, which is where this
repository keeps every accepted plan including the two authorizing this work.
Reproduced live: on a branch carrying a committed, accepted plan, the plan gate
still answered ask. Package 4, and it should land even if the risk-tiering half
of that package is dropped, because it is not a risk-tiering change.

codev --version cannot distinguish a source snapshot from the tree it came
from -- a 31 August snapshot, main three waves later, and PyPI's actual latest
release all reported different-or-equal numbers with no way to tell. That is
how 496 gate calls failed open unnoticed after the hooks became shims in
57bde9c. Package 6, with the 0.6.0 cut.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

refactor(navigator)!: rename the oracle to the navigator

Package 1 of the developer-experience plan, and deliberately a rename and
nothing else so the packages after it read as behavior diffs.

The name comes from the half of a driver/navigator pair that does not have
hands on the keyboard, which is exactly this module's job: it says where the
work stands and what comes next, and never acts. In a pair slice (ADR-0038)
the metaphor stops being decorative -- the developer drives and this navigates.
'Consult the oracle' also invited the reading that the answer is unexplained,
which is the opposite of what a module returning a reason with every answer is
for.

guidance and workflow were considered and rejected: an agent consults a
navigator but merely reads guidance, and workflow collides with the package
name codev_workflow.

Public behavior is unchanged. codev next keeps its spelling, every NextAction
field keeps its name, and the thirteen-outcome table is untouched -- the whole
suite passes without a single test assertion changing.

Not renamed: ADR-0036 and ADR-0037, which are append-only; the unified-workflow
brief and implementation plan, which are historical records of what was decided
at the time; and audit-google-python-style's 'verifier or oracle script', which
is the unrelated test-oracle sense of the word.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(cli): add the composite slice and round verbs

Package 2 of the developer-experience plan. ADR-0036 established that the CLI
is an agent interface; this finishes the thought, because an interface whose
correct use needs a twenty-five-line protocol is a procedure, not an interface.

Four verbs, each replacing one numbered step in a role file that issued
several commands with conditional flags between them:

codev slice begin -- branch, GitHub issue, and round state in one call. It
replaces codev git branch, an issue-existence check, codev git issue-create,
codev task start with three mutually exclusive linkage flags, and the codev
task relink recovery path for an issue that arrived late. Branch first and
issue second, deliberately: both orders can fail partway, and this one leaves
a local branch with no round state, which codev next reports and a developer
can delete, rather than an issue on GitHub that nothing points at.

codev round close -- commit and record the round against the exact resulting
head. Named for its caller, not its subject: only whoever holds commit
permission can know that head, which is precisely why a builder never records
its own round, and a verb spelled 'record --role builder' invites the call the
design forbids. The round number is derived from state rather than passed,
because a caller that guesses it wrong silently writes into the wrong slot.

codev slice publish -- push and open the draft pull request. The body is
always the task's rendered evidence, so the old 'never pass --body' caveat
now has no way to be violated rather than being documented more loudly.

codev slice land -- advance to the next slice, or close the task when this was
the last. Which one applies is a fact about the slice list, not a decision the
caller should be making.

Nothing is removed. The granular git and task verbs these compose are still
there for recovery paths and for a mid-session agent that needs one step
alone, and the composites call the same git_ops and task functions rather than
reimplementing them -- the plan's stop condition was that a composite needing
logic which does not already exist is a new capability in disguise.

The issue-linkage rule is extracted to _resolve_linkage and now has one
implementation that both task start and slice begin call, rather than two
copies free to drift about when a task may exist without an issue.

codev issue draft, the fifth verb the plan listed, is deliberately not added.
Its only remaining caller after slice begin exists is the planner's issue-only
short circuit, and codev git issue-create --body-file already does exactly
that job. The caveat it was meant to remove is removed by deleting prose in
package 5, not by adding a synonym.

The gh stub grows issue create, and issue view now answers for issues the stub
was actually told about instead of a fixed placeholder.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(navigator): answer for the whole lifecycle, and stop dead-ending

Package 3 of the developer-experience plan. Navigator coverage goes from six
uncovered steps of nine to zero of eight, measured by the walk landed in #33.

The planning phases get positions. Every state before a task existed collapsed
into one sentence -- 'pick up an issue and start a task' -- which left the
whole Understand, Design and Plan half unguided, and that is the half where a
developer has the least context and the most to decide. The navigator now
resolves brief, design, wave plan, and plan from the artifacts a repository
actually holds, reading the Status: line those artifacts already carry rather
than introducing a metadata format for anyone to keep in step. A drafted plan
is reported as blocking its own downstream work, because recommending work
that nothing authorizes is worse than saying what is missing.

Blocked positions carry options. Each is a label, a command, and what choosing
it means. No authority moves -- choosing is still a human's job -- but a stop
that offers 'absorb the change as pair work' alongside 'escalate' reads as a
decision rather than a wall, and every one of those escapes already existed.

GitHub is consulted for any position where a pull request could exist, not
only the two reasons that imply human review. That restriction is why a
merged slice sitting at ok_ready_for_pr was told to open a pull request it had
already merged.

ok_waiting_on_reviewer is split into the three states it conflated. task.check
cannot tell a freshly opened round from one whose builder has reported --
neither has a reviewer verdict -- so the single entry recommended the reviewer
in every case, including before any work existed. An agent that follows that
reviews an empty diff. The two facts that separate them are local and cheap: a
builder receipt on the current round, and whether the worktree holds
uncommitted work. It counts product paths only, or opening round state would
make every fresh slice look like it already had work waiting.

A draft pull request is no longer reported as awaiting human review. Nobody
can review a draft; mark-ready is what requests it, and nothing the navigator
said ever named that step.

Recommendations now name the composite verbs from package 2, which is what
actually moves the measure -- package 2 built them and this points at them, so
neither package moves the number alone.

Not renamed to a composite: 'branch exists, no round state' still recommends
codev task start, because slice begin creates the branch and the branch is
what already exists. That position is the recovery path, and recovery needs
the granular verb.

The baseline records why nine steps became eight: slice begin collapsed two
transitions into one. That is the lifecycle getting shorter, not the walk
skipping a step.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(gate)!: risk-tier the plan gate, and let it see this repo's plans

Package 4 of the developer-experience plan, and the one that trades ceremony
for ergonomics deliberately.

The plan gate keyed purely on a file existing, so it asked the same question
of a one-file bug fix and a subsystem rewrite. Ceremony that cannot tell those
apart does not produce plans; it teaches agents to route around the gate.

It now tiers, as a changed default rather than a configuration key. Within the
slice's size budget on a task branch, the focus card in the conversation
satisfies it. Past the budget it asks again. Dependency and environment
manifests, CI workflow definitions, and migrations ask regardless of size --
a one-line version bump changes what the code computes, which for research
software surfaces as an unreproducible result rather than an outage; a
workflow file decides whether anything is checked at all; a migration is
irreversible against real data. A repository-mutating git command is never
tiered: a push is not made safe by the change being small.

This reads as a weakening and is not, because of when the gate fires. It runs
before an edit, so the only diff it can see is the one already on the branch.
The old gate interrupted before the work started, when a developer knows least
about what the change will need. This one interrupts when the change outgrows
what a focus card can carry. Toll booth to tripwire.

Two holes found while building it, both closed. codev task size answers with
zeros and over_budget=false for a task that does not exist, and for one whose
state carries no base to diff against; either would have let any branch merely
named codev/... skip the gate entirely. A measurement of nothing is not a
measurement of a small change, so the tier requires real round state with a
real base before believing the number.

Size is now measured in-process. Shelling out to codev task size dated from
the hooks being standalone scripts outside the package; with the gates living
in codev_workflow it made both of them depend on a codev being on PATH and
being the same build -- the same class of silent failure that let 496 gate
calls pass unchecked.

_SPEC_GLOBS finally covers docs/plans/*.md, where this repository keeps every
accepted plan including the ones authorizing this work. A guardrail that
cannot see the artifact it asks for teaches agents the artifact is pointless.
This half is not a risk-tiering change and stands on its own.

No existing gate test had to be converted from ask to allow. The plan required
each to be re-examined individually rather than in bulk; every one still
asserts what it always did, which is the strongest evidence the tier is
additive rather than a blanket relaxation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

refactor(agents)!: lead replaces orchestrator and planner

The installed copies of the role, guideline, and integration files, updated for
ADR-0040 alongside their bundle sources. Separate commit because codev git
commit refuses to mix CoDev-managed paths with product changes in one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(agents)!: collapse three human-facing agents into lead

Package 5 of the developer-experience plan, and the clause of the
unified-workflow brief's item 8 that never shipped: 'the three sessions
collapse into one run ... because a session boundary the developer has to
notice is a command by another name'.

orchestrator becomes lead, the only agent a developer talks to. planner is
removed: roughly forty of its fifty-six lines routed to skills lead now
invokes directly, codev next computes the routing its Scope section described
in prose, and its one unique behavior -- the issue-only short circuit -- is
codev git issue-create --body-file. outer-loop-runner keeps its file and loses
its trigger; it holds irreducible protocol that folding into lead would
reproduce as the long role file this package exists to remove, so lead
dispatches it, permission-gated like the specialists (ADR-0021).

Thirteen roles become eleven. Three human-facing roles become one, which is
the number that matters.

lead.md's body is 69 lines against orchestrator.md's 167, inside the 80-line
budget without needing the lead-protocol skill the plan held in reserve. That
budget was the test of whether packages 2 and 3 went far enough, and they did:
the ten-step build protocol is four composite verbs, and the routing prose is
a codev next call.

Two migration defects found by dogfooding the update on this repository, both
fixed rather than documented.

A retired role file was retained, not deleted -- 'upstream removed; retained
locally'. That is right for a doc and wrong for a role: every adapter treats a
file in its agents directory as an invocable agent, so an existing
installation would have ended up with orchestrator.md beside lead.md, which is
exactly the confusion this consolidation removes. An untouched retired role is
now deleted; a locally edited one stays a conflict the developer resolves.

A retired OpenCode agent left its hash in the lock forever, because the
reconciliation loop only iterated the agents that still ship. codev status
reported drift that no update could resolve. Retired agents now leave both the
config and the lock, with the same edited-means-conflict policy.

OpenCode's default_agent migrates from orchestrator to lead rather than being
preserved as a local change, because the old value names an agent that no
longer ships.

Four ADRs record the decisions of packages 1 through 4 -- 0040 the lead agent,
0041 composite verbs, 0042 the navigator, 0043 the risk-tiered gate. ADR-0030
and ADR-0031 are resolved from Proposed to Accepted rather than left
indefinite while later ADRs build on them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs: describe the tool that now exists, and cut 0.6.0

Package 6, the last of the developer-experience plan.

The documentation site, product map, and CLI reference described three
human-facing agents and a developer who chose between them. They describe one
agent now. The roles page leads with lead and says plainly what changed and
why; the tutorials and starting prompts stop telling anyone to switch sessions.
Two passages needed rewriting rather than renaming -- a blind substitution had
produced 'lead for build work, lead for anything upstream' and 'lead never
invokes lead', which is what happens when a rename touches prose that was
about the distinction being removed.

codev --version reports the commit for a source install: 0.6.0+source.abc1234.
Two trees reporting the same version is how a build installed from source in
August kept claiming 0.5.0 while main moved three waves ahead of it, and why
496 gate calls failed open against a codev gate subcommand it did not have.

codev self update no longer tells a source install to fetch a release. uv tool
upgrade resolves against the index, whose latest release was 0.4.0 the whole
time -- advice that silently downgrades the tool it is meant to update. It now
detects a source checkout and says how to update that instead.

0.5.0 becomes 0.6.0. This is breaking: role files are renamed and removed, and
planner disappears as an invocable agent. CoDev is pre-1.0, and phase-6's
reading stands -- in the 0.x line the minor version is the breaking-change
boundary. The changelog's Upgrading section says what codev update does to an
existing installation, including that it stops and asks rather than discarding
a retired role you edited.

fix(ci): three failures the local suite could not see

packaging/BUILD.bazel carries a third copy of the version, beside
pyproject.toml and __init__.py, and release-integrity compares all three. The
0.6.0 bump missed it.

tests/test_adapter.py was edited by script and never reformatted, which
fmt-check caught and my ruff run did not, because I formatted the files I
wrote rather than the ones I touched.

RiskTieredPlanGateTests built a repository and committed into it without
configuring an identity, so every test in the class errored in setUp with git
exit 128. This passed locally only because a developer machine has a global
git identity and a CI runner has none -- the existing integration Sandbox
already sets one, and the new helper did not follow it. Verified by running
the whole suite with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL and GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM pointed at
/dev/null, which reproduces the runner and now passes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(test): annotate the composite-verb helper's return type

tests/test_composite_verbs.py's run() returned a bare dict, which mypy rejects
under this project's settings. Both quality and release-integrity run the type
check, so one missing annotation failed two jobs.

Found by CI rather than locally because I ran mypy on the files I had just
edited instead of the check the repository actually defines. Verified this time
with mypy over src and tests together, which is what CI runs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(ci): update verify-dist's hardcoded bundled-agent list

A fourth place the role set is written down, after ADAPTER_ROLE_PATHS,
OPENCODE_AGENT_CONFIGS, and the installer tests: verify-dist asserts the exact
filenames shipped inside the wheel, and still expected orchestrator.md and
planner.md.

The assertion is worth keeping -- it catches a role that silently fails to be
packaged, which no unit test would see because they all read the source tree
rather than the built wheel. Checked against the bundle directory rather than
retyped.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(test): stop test_git_ops racing its own teardown

The same teardown race fixed for the integration Sandbox, in the file that
makes its own temporary directories rather than using it: TemporaryDirectory
cleanup removing a tree git was still writing into, raising 'Directory not
empty' on ubuntu/3.11 after every assertion in the test had passed.

Fixed at the cause rather than the symptom, and in one place rather than
ninety-four: gc.auto=0 in _init_repo, which every repository in the file goes
through, and on the four bare origins, which are pushed into and so are where a
background repack is most likely.
